amendments.rule: The conjunction `וְ` is normally English *and*, including the waw of a consecutive verb form: the conjunction takes *And* and the verb takes the verb. Where the ASV renders it by some other connective, align it to that word instead. **The list is open and is read off the ASV rather than checked against a set**: the corpus already aligns a waw to *but*, *then*, *so*, *or*, *now*, *also*, *for*, *therefore*, *neither*, *nor*, *yea*, *yet*, *even*, *with*, *moreover* and *howbeit*, among others. A connective the ASV has written for a waw is never `added`, and it is never folded into a neighbouring word to avoid one: a town list writes *with* for the waw of `וְחַצְרֵיהֶן` → *with their villages* and *even* for the waw of `וָיָמָּה` → *even unto the sea*, and each waw takes the word written for it. Read what stands in the clause for that waw in particular, as rule 51 requires for *also*, and where the ASV leaves it unrendered, mark it `unrepresented`.
amendments.why: Rule 14's four-word list reads as closed, and rule 51 had already to be written because one word outside it — *also* — kept being marked `added`. JOS.15 renders the waw by *with* in twelve units (15.32, 36, 41, 44, 46, 51, 54, 57, 59, 60, 62), by *even* (15.46), *now* (15.15), *but* (15.63), *also* (15.19) and *and so* (15.7), none of them in the list. The corpus carries every one of these in quantity — 63 *so*, 58 *also*, 48 *with*, 41 *for*, 36 *therefore*, 23 *yea*, 19 *yet*, 17 *even* — so nothing contradicts the widening and the closed reading is what the evidence contradicts. The amendment changes only the second sentence and keeps the unrendered clause and rule 51's cross-reference intact.

amendments.rule: The definite direct-object marker `אֵת` (H853) has no English realization of its own and is normally its own `unrepresented` unit; that is the ruling on the large majority of its occurrences. It takes English only where the ASV spends a word on the object relation itself and no other morpheme licenses that word. Three families qualify. An English verb may reach its object through a preposition — *hearken unto*, *spake unto*, *inquire of*, *fight against*, *send for* — where that preposition exists only to attach the object to the verb; it is the marker's rendering, not the object noun's, and the marker heads on it. An appositional or resumptive marker may be rendered *even* or *to wit*. And a marker on an object the ASV fronts before its clause and resumes inside it with a pronoun may be rendered *as for*: `וְאֶת־הַיְבוּסִי יוֹשְׁבֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם לֹא־יָכְלוּ בְנֵי־יְהוּדָה לְהוֹרִישָׁם` → *And* ***as for*** *the Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out* gives *as for* to the marker, headed on *as* by rule 24, since the resuming *them* is the suffix's under rule 18 and nothing else answers to the two words. Test by subtraction: drop the English word and ask which morpheme has lost its rendering. If nothing but the object relation is diminished, the marker takes the word; if the ASV writes the object bare — *he built the house* — the marker is `unrepresented`. Do not confuse H853 with its homograph the preposition `אֵת` *with* (H854), which is an ordinary preposition aligning by rule 11.
amendments.why: JOS.15.63 fronts the marked object and resumes it with the suffix on the infinitive, and the ASV spends *as for* on that relation alone. Rule 16's operative subtraction test awards those words to the marker, but the enumerative sentence 'Two families qualify' closes the set against them and would force `unrepresented` marker plus `added` *as for* — English no morpheme licenses, which rule 30 reserves for something else. The corpus renders `אֵת` by an object-relation word in 120 of 1155 units (*even*, *to wit*, *unto*, *for*, *of*, *at*, *in*, *against*, *on*, *toward*) and carries no unit rendering it *as for* under any competing analysis, so nothing contradicts the third family. The amendment adds one family and its worked example and leaves the rest of the rule, including the H854 warning, unchanged.

conventions: `הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל` → *the great sea* (JOS.15.12, JOS.15.47): the phrase holds two article morphemes and the ASV writes a single *the*, standing before *great*. The attributive's article takes it and the article on `יָם` is `unrepresented`. This is the same test the chapter applies to `יָם הַמֶּלַח` → *the Salt Sea* at JOS.15.2 and JOS.15.5 under rule 29 — the written *the* goes to the article morpheme standing on the English word it precedes, and is fronted only where that word is rendered anarthrously. BSB reads the *the* onto the noun's article instead; that is the competing analysis and it accounts for two of this chapter's thirteen Td disagreements.

`וּגְבוּל` → *and the border thereof* (JOS.15.12, JOS.15.47): the italicized *thereof* is its own `added` unit in both verses. `גְּבוּל` carries no pronominal suffix in either, so no morpheme licenses the word, and it is not to be folded onto the noun as a helper (rules 7, 30).

report: Cross-verse: all 69 candidate groups read against the dumps. Every bucket with two treatments traces to a word the ASV actually writes differently, or to a morpheme that is present in one place and absent in the other. No split found, so patches is empty.

waw before Ncbpc (14 occurrences, 2 treatments) is the largest candidate and is not a split: the ASV writes 'with their villages' in the eleven count-formula verses and 'and its villages' at JOS.15.45 and 15.47 (twice), where a second waw already carried the 'with'. Read against the ASV text in each verse.

min + negeb at JOS.15.3 is fused to 'southward' at its first occurrence and split as 'by' / 'the south' at its second, which the verse's own review note records; the same test governs mi-qtseh, fused to 'uttermost' at JOS.15.21 where the ASV spends one word and split as 'at/from the uttermost part' at JOS.15.1, 15.2, 15.5 and 15.8. Rule 30's one-English-rendering condition accounts for both, not a chapter inconsistency.

Directive he has three treatments and all three are ASV-driven: it takes a written directional word (to, at, unto: 15.3, 15.4, 15.7, 15.11, 15.12, 15.46), it fuses where the ASV writes one word (southward, northward, westward: 15.1, 15.7, 15.8, 15.10, 15.11), and it is unrepresented where the ASV writes only the plain compass noun (15.5 twice, 15.10, 15.21). Where no he is present the supplied to/by/at joins the place name under rule 33 (15.6, 15.9, 15.10, 15.11), which is why those verses look different and are not.

Construct-chain the's are counted the same way throughout: fronted onto the article where the rectum is rendered anarthrously (15.13 'the father of Anak', 15.14 'the three sons of Anak', 15.62 'the City of Salt'), standing before its own word where the rectum is arthrous (15.4, 15.5, 15.8, 15.9, 15.11, 15.19), and supplied to the construct where no article morpheme is in the chain (15.1, 15.20, 15.21). That is rule 29 applied consistently, not three analyses.

ha-yam ha-gadol at JOS.15.12 and JOS.15.47 is aligned identically in both verses and each verse cross-references the other: the single written 'the' stands before 'great', so the attributive's article takes it and the article on yam is unrepresented. Recorded as a convention because it is a genuine tie that BSB reads the other way.

BSB: none of the 30 disagreements is an error. R x 9 are prepositions the ASV's recasting silences (dative lahem/lakem read as a possessive at 15.2 and 15.4, bare indirect objects at 15.17 and 15.19, the unrendered le before the infinitive at 15.63, el before the fused 'southward' at 15.3) - rule 40, and BSB attaches them to their phrase. Td x 13 are articles on toponyms where the ASV writes no 'the' (15.3, 15.7, 15.11, 15.34, 15.36, 15.38, 15.57, 15.60, 15.62), the two ha-yam ha-gadol articles, and the two articles of 'unto this day' at 15.63, which rule 29's own 'these cities' example marks unrepresented. Sd x 4 are directive he's with nothing written for them. The four singletons: eth at 15.14 is rule 16's majority ruling; the apodosis waw at 15.16 is unwritten; lah after 'said' at 15.18 has no English pronoun in the verse; the paragogic he of tenah at 15.19 is rule 32's first sentence.

Conventions: two recorded (the ha-yam ha-gadol article, and the italic 'thereof' of u-gebul as added in both 15.12 and 15.47). The other 63 repeated notes restate contract rules already binding every verse and are left out of the log deliberately.

Amendments: rule 14, because its four-word list reads closed and this chapter renders the waw by 'with' twelve times and by 'even', 'now', 'but', 'also' and 'and so' besides, all of which the corpus carries in quantity; and rule 16, because 'Two families qualify' would force the wrong answer on the fronted, resumed object marker at JOS.15.63 rendered 'as for', which rule 16's own subtraction test awards to the marker. No new rules proposed.
